jobs.title: Data Engineer - People Analytics
jobs.description: We’re building a world of health around every individual — shaping a more connected, convenient and compassionate health experience. At CVS Health®, you’ll be surrounded by passionate colleagues who care deeply, innovate with purpose, hold ourselves accountable and prioritize safety and quality in everything we do. Join us and be part of something bigger – helping to simplify health care one person, one family and one community at a time. Position Summary The Data Engineer - People Analytics role is a technical developer in IT and individual contributor for the People Analytics Data Engineering team responsible for the development of data warehouse modeling, data pipelines, and related analytics specific to People and Workforce analytics in cloud data platforms. Key Responsibilities Data Pipeline Management Design, build, and manage robust data pipelines and ETL processes that integrate HR data from various systems, including Workday, talent management, payroll, and other data sources. Data Engineering and Transformation Develop and optimize data workflows to ensure data accuracy, quality, and availability for the People Analytics team and stakeholders across HR and business units. Technical Leadership Oversee a team of data engineers, providing mentorship, support, and guidance on best practices in data engineering, version control, and coding standards. Analytics & Reporting Support Work closely with People Analytics to structure data for analysis, develop data models, and create reproducible workflows that enable efficient reporting in R, Python, and other analytics tools. Data Security and Compliance Ensure data governance and security protocols are followed in accordance with company policies and industry regulations, with a focus on HR data confidentiality and compliance. Collaboration with Stakeholders Partner with HR leaders, IT, and People Analytics teams to understand business requirements, streamline data requests, and provide insights to support strategic decisions. Required Qualifications 3+ years' experience in Data Engineering 3+ years' experience with ETL/ELT processes and tools. 3+ years' experience with SQL and relational databases. 2+ years' experience programming in Python for data manipulation, automation, and analysis. 3+ years' experience with cloud platforms, prefer GCP (may consider Azure or AWS). 2+ years' experience with data warehousing solutions (e.g., Snowflake, Redshift, BigQuery). 2+ years' experience with scheduling tools like Airflow or Composer. Preferred Qualifications Experience with Workday or similar HRIS platforms and data flows within an HR context. Problem-Solving ability and strong analytical skills with the ability to troubleshoot, optimize, and automate data processes. Strong communication skills with the ability to communicate complex technical processes to non-technical stakeholders effectively. Familiarity or working knowledge of common data visualization or business intelligence tools (PowerBI, Tableau, Oracle BI, Visier, etc.). Preferably technical experience specific to people or talent analytics, data engineering, visualization, business intelligence, or analytical consulting. Education Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Data Engineering, Data Science, or a related field required. Master's degree preferred. Anticipated Weekly Hours 40 Time Type Full time Pay Range The Typical Pay Range For This Role Is $83,430.00 - $222,480.00 This pay range represents the base hourly rate or base annual full-time salary for all positions in the job grade within which this position falls. The actual base salary offer will depend on a variety of factors including experience, education, geography and other relevant factors. This position is eligible for a CVS Health bonus, commission or short-term incentive program in addition to the base pay range listed above. Our people fuel our future. Our teams reflect the customers, patients, members and communities we serve and we are committed to fostering a workplace where every colleague feels valued and that they belong. Great Benefits For Great People We take pride in offering a comprehensive and competitive mix of pay and benefits that reflects our commitment to our colleagues and their families. This full‑time position is eligible for a comprehensive benefits package designed to support the physical, emotional, and financial well‑being of colleagues and their families. The benefits for this position include medical, dental, and vision coverage, paid time off, retirement savings options, wellness programs, and other resources, based on eligibility. Additional details about available benefits are provided during the application process and on Benefits Moments. We anticipate the application window for this opening will close on: 10/22/2026 Qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment in accordance with all federal, state and local laws.

jobs.title: Institutional Data Engineer
jobs.description: Department: IT Enterprise Applications Advertised Salary Range Part/Full Time: Full Time About UofSC From the Upstate to the Lowcountry, the University of South Carolina system is transforming the lives of South Carolinians through the impact of our eight institutions and 20 locations throughout the state. More than 50,000 students are enrolled at one of eight institutions, including the research campus in Columbia and comprehensive four-year universities in Aiken, Upstate and Beaufort. In addition, our Palmetto College campuses in Salkehatchie, Union, Lancaster and Sumter enable students to earn associate or bachelor's degrees through a combination of in-person, online or blended learning. All of our system institutions place strong emphasis on service — helping to build healthier, more educated communities in South Carolina and beyond. Inclusive Excellence Statement Advertised Job Summary Shape the Future of Data Analytics at One of America's Most Beautiful Campuses Join the University of South Carolina in Columbia, the vibrant capital city of one of the fastest-growing states in the nation. As we revolutionize our digital landscape, we are seeking an experienced Institutional Data Engineer to join our Analytics and Data Governance team within the Division of Information Technology. Help us transform South Carolina's flagship campus into a nationally recognized hub for innovation and data-driven excellence. This is an opportunity to make a meaningful difference while working with evolving technologies and solving challenging problems in a collaborative environment. The Institutional Data Engineer serves as a technical expert responsible for designing, developing, maintaining, and optimizing the University's enterprise data infrastructure, integration processes, and analytical data environments. This role integrates data from multiple enterprise systems, develops and maintains data pipelines, supports data quality and governance initiatives, and enables reliable institutional analytics and reporting for the University of South Carolina and its extended campuses. Key Responsibilities Provide scalable and reliable access to institutional data. Improve data accuracy, completeness, and consistency. Modernize the institution's analytics capabilities. What We're Looking For Strong problem-solving and communication skills; works well across distributed teams. Demonstrated proficiency in data engineering technologies and processes (e.g., SQL, relational databases, ETL/ELT technologies, data warehousing) Brings strategic vision and operational excellence to IT service delivery. Thrives in a collaborative culture where curiosity and innovation are valued. Why Join Us? Join a collaborative team that supports innovation and service-oriented technology solutions. Solve data challenges that have meaningful institutional and system-wide impacts. Help shape the university's analytics capabilities, data-informed culture, and institutional decision-making. Perks of the University of South Carolina Join a major public research university with opportunities to work on complex, meaningful technology and data initiatives. Collaborate with talented professionals across the university system. Enjoy a professional environment that emphasizes innovation, continuous learning, collaboration, and technical excellence. Work in a role that offers opportunities to contribute to the strategic and operational success of the university. Preferred Qualifications Minimum Qualifications (Classified and Unclassified positions) Bachelor's degree in Data Analytics, Information Systems, Computer Science, Statistics, or a related field. Strong proficiency in ETL tools (e.g., IBM DataStorage, Informatica, SSIS) and BI tools (e.g., Cognos, Tableau, PowerBI), including recommended configuration and security practices in hardware and cloud-based server environments. Strong proficiency in SQL for data querying, transformation, and optimization. Experience with relational databases such as Oracle, SQL Server, or PostgreSQL. Familiarity with data warehouse concepts and dimensional modeling. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with keen attention to detail. Excellent communication skills and the ability to work collaboratively in a team environment. Experience working in a higher education or public sector environment. Experience working with enterprise data systems (e.g., HR, Finance, Student Information, Learning Management) and large-scale institutional datasets. Knowledge/Skills/Abilities Knowledge of higher education data structures, business processes, and institutional research methodologies. Ability to follow directions and communicate effectively with colleagues and supervisors. Ability to collaborate across distributed, cross-functional teams. jobs.description: Come join Analog Devices (ADI) – a place where Innovation meets Impact. For more than 55 years, Analog Devices has been inventing new breakthrough technologies that transform lives. At ADI you will work alongside the brightest minds to collaborate on solving complex problems that matter from autonomous vehicles, drones and factories to augmented reality and remote healthcare. ADI fosters a culture that focuses on employees through beneficial programs, aligned goals, continuous learning opportunities, and practices that create a more sustainable future. About Analog Devices Analog Devices, Inc. (NASDAQ: ADI) is a global semiconductor leader that bridges the physical and digital worlds to enable breakthroughs at the Intelligent Edge. ADI combines analog, digital, AI, and software technologies into solutions that combat climate change, reliably connect humans and the world, and help drive advancements in automation and robotics, mobility, healthcare, energy and data centers. With revenue of more than $11 billion in FY25, ADI ensures today's innovators stay Ahead of What's Possible. Learn more at www.analog.com and on LinkedIn and X. Summary: ADI is solving complex challenges that require greater visibility into programs throughout the development lifecycle. As an operations analyst, you will collect and analyze information related to software projects and digital SoCs, maintaining clear record of program status and identifying risks, gaps, and dependencies. This role will collaborate with product management, engineering, and project management to generate clear insights into project and portfolio health.
